public_body: Captain Samuel Brown Elementary School Council
overall: The AG found the Council violated the Open Meeting Law by posting one annual notice per school year with only two generic topics; it declined the public-records minutes-access claim and ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council failed to properly post notice for its 2021-2022 and 2022-2023 school year meetings.
allegations.key_passage: This is entirely insufficient to comply with the requirement of the Open Meeting Law that meeting notices include a list of the topics that the chair, or other individual authorized to create the notice, reasonably anticipates, 48 hours in advance, will be discussed at the meeting

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Council failed to comply with 950 CMR 32.05(1)(f) on electronic access to meeting minutes, a Public Records Law regulation.
allegations.key_passage: Because this allegation concerns the Council’s compliance with the Public Records Law and its regulations, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Not raised in the complaint: the AG found the Council's minutes insufficient, listing topics without attendance, documents, discussion summaries, decisions, or votes.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, the minutes do not summarize any of the discussions that occurred and do not record any of the decisions made or actions or votes taken.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (order)
Amend past meeting minutes to the best of its ability in accordance with the guidance provided (recommendation, not an order)
remedy_passage: We order the Council’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a future similar violation may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
